text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA
- Serbian and Montenegrin Presidents Slobodan Milosevic and Momir Bulatovic agree maintaining the federal republic of Yugoslavia is in the vital interst of the Serb and Montenegrin peoples.
- Rally of Serb-French friendship was held in Zemun attended by head of the National Front of France Jean-Marie Le Pen, who is visiting Belgrade as a guest of the Serbian Radical Party.

- There could be an exodus of Serbs from Eastern Slavonia in Croatia if they do not get additional guarantees from the Croatian govenrment, says president of the Serb government of the region Vojislav Stanimirovic.
- Nine Serbian shipyards are on an export offensive and look at achieving excellent results in 1997, says Jezdimir Arsic of the Serbian chamber of economy.
- Alcatel of France and Serbian postal company PTT sign a two-year, $40 million deal to provide 300,000 new telephone lines.

- The oil industry tops Yugoslavia's wage scale with an average wage of 2,122 dinars in December while the bottom is held by the leather and footwear industry with 339 dinars, says Yugoslav statistical office. (Average wage in December was 881 dinars).

- There will be sufficient quantities of wheat and flour until the next harvest and no measures are being taken for import of these commodities according to Serbian directorate for commodity reserves.

- Municipal electoral commission for Belgrade confirms another nine councillor mandates for the municipal council. Opposition coalition Zajedno now has 65, the left coalition 27, the radical party 16 and the Democratic Party of Serbia 2 seats in the city council.

- Belgrade city transport (GSP) independent trade union fails to reach agreement in talks with management and will start strike on midnight Thursday if no progress is made in more talks scheduled today.
NASA BORBA
- Protesters continue to gather in streets, students stay non stop in front of police cordons over annulled election results.
- Several thousand people from Kragujevac protest in front of TV building because old management refuses to leave and allow the new management to take over.
- Macedonian-Yugoslav commission on implementation of the free-trade agreement suspends work over disagreement on black metallurgy contingents.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Serbian-ethnic Albanian talks on Kosovo end in Munich, the sides agree to draw up programme for further work.
- First day of ex-Yugoslavia succession talks in Brussels centre on defining state property.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Trade union of metal workers of Serbia announces series of protests unless public enterprises repay debts of more than 200 million dinars (around $37 million) owed to the sector.
- Yugoslav finance minister Tomica Raicevic receives delegation of Banque Nationale de Paris.
